Prototype walkthrough · film 1 of 1

The evidence file a chatbot cannot assemble

Most readers evaluating an idea already pay for a frontier chatbot, and IDEA_ANALYSIS §5 says the honest response is to feed it rather than compete with it. A finished report now hands its whole self over as Markdown — every claim with the verbatim span it came from, every source with a URL and a date. Rendered in Rust rather than in the browser, because the page already draws this data and a second renderer would hold a second opinion about what a source’s standing is called. Quotes lose their line breaks and nothing else; the size bound names the sections it dropped rather than stopping halfway. Running it against a real company found what no test would have: the provenance line was printing the inference server’s address, in the one document written to be pasted into somebody else’s service.

The full source is in the pull request. github.com/larry94555/competitive-landscape

All the films

  • 1. The evidence file a chatbot cannot assemblenow playing
The recording has no audio. Subtitles are on by default, so it reads fine muted. Narration is optional and spoken by your browser — and it sets the pace: the video pauses while each line is read, then continues, so nothing is cut off mid-sentence.

To pause: press space, click the picture, or use the button in the bar. Any of the three stops the narration too — otherwise the voice would keep talking over a still frame.

This is a prototype, not the product. Invented companies on the reserved .example domain, no working system behind it, throwaway code. It exists to answer one question before any production code is written: does a 90–180 second wait read as work happening, or as a hang?
